# Job Chapter 6 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 418r–418v

---

**1** Then Job replied:

**2** "If only my misery could be weighed
and all my suffering placed on the scales!

**3** It would be heavier than the sand of the seas —
no wonder my words have been so wild.

**4** For the arrows of the Almighty have pierced me;
my spirit is drinking in their poison;
God's terrors are lined up against me.

**5** Does a wild donkey bray when it has grass?
Does an ox bellow when it has feed?

**6** Can tasteless food be eaten without salt?
Is there any flavor in the white of an egg?

**7** I refuse to touch such food;
it makes me sick to even look at it.

**8** Oh, if only God would grant my one request,
give me the one thing I hope for:

**9** that he would be willing to crush me,
to reach out his hand and end my life!

**10** That would be my comfort —
I would even rejoice in unrelenting pain —
for I have never denied the words of the Holy One.

**11** But what strength do I have left to keep waiting?
What is ahead for me that I should hold on?

**12** Am I made of stone?
Is my body made of bronze?

**13** I have no resources left within me;
every capacity for coping has been driven away.

**14** A despairing person deserves loyalty from his friends,
even if he has abandoned the fear of the Almighty.

**15** But my brothers have been as unreliable as a desert stream —
as a river bed that overflows one season

**16** and runs dark with melting ice and snow,

**17** but dries up in the heat
and vanishes from its channel when the weather turns warm.

**18** Caravans leave the main road to look for water there;
they wander into the wasteland and die.

**19** The caravans of Tema search for them;
the travelers of Sheba look with hope.

**20** But they are bitterly disappointed;
they arrive at the spot and find nothing.

**21** That is what you have become to me — nothing.
You see my terrible condition and you recoil in fear.

**22** Have I ever asked you for a handout?
Have I begged you to pay a ransom from your wealth?

**23** Have I asked you to rescue me from an enemy
or save me from the grip of the ruthless?

**24** Teach me, and I will be quiet.
Show me where I have gone wrong.

**25** Honest words carry real weight!
But your arguments — what do they actually prove?

**26** Are you going to pick apart the words of a desperate man,
treating his cries of anguish as nothing but hot air?

**27** You would gamble away an orphan
and sell your own friend for profit!

**28** Now look me in the face —
would I lie to you?

**29** Reconsider! Don't be unjust.
Reconsider! My integrity is on the line.

**30** Is there anything false in what I'm saying?
Can't I tell the difference between right and wrong?"

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**"Heavier than the sand of the seas" (vv.2-3):** Job's opening metaphor is his answer to Eliphaz. He is not being "impatient" (4:5) — his grief is immeasurable, and his wild words are proportional to his suffering. This is one of the Bible's most important statements about the relationship between pain and expression: extreme suffering produces extreme speech.

**The wadi metaphor (vv.15-20):** Job transforms a geographical reality into a devastating indictment. Desert streams are full when no one needs them and empty when they are desperately needed. The friends came to comfort (2:11) but offer only theology. They are winter floods to a summer traveler.

**"Teach me and I will be quiet" (v.24):** This is Job's direct challenge. He does not claim perfection — he asks his friends to name his sin. Their inability to do so exposes the weakness of their entire argument: they assume sin but cannot identify it.

---
*— PNEUMA*
